newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish H1 trade gap up to $5.39 bln - Stats office.
newsitem.headline: Polish H1 trade gap up to $5.39 bln - Stats office.

text.p: Poland's registered trade gap in the first six months of 1996 amounted to $5.39 billion, more than double the $2.57 billion deficit during the first half of 1995, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said on Friday.
GUS' registered trade figures are compiled using customs receipts and do not include large cross-border trade inflows, which balance Poland's current account flows.
GUS said registered exports during the January-June period were 7.2-percent higher than in the same period last year, while imports were 26.8-percent higher than a year earlier.
According to the National Bank of Poland's trade data, based on bank flows, Poland had a $3.15 billion merchandise trade gap in this period.
POLISH TRADE BALANCE JAN-JUNE JAN-MAY JAN-JULY 95
